epithet: Two kingdoms, and what they did with their blessings
lede: The house of Dāwūd was given iron that bent in the hand and wind that carried a month’s journey in a morning, and was told: work, in thanks. The people of Sabaʾ were given two gardens and a forgiving Lord, and turned away. One story is of gratitude and the other of a flood.

names.name: Sabaʾ
names.note: After the people of its fifteenth ayah: the kingdom of southern Arabia whose prosperity rested on the great dam of Maʾrib. It is one of five surahs that open with “Praise be to Allah”.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of all. One ayah is differed over, the sixth — “those given knowledge see that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth”: some said it is Makkan and means the believing Companions, as Ibn ʿAbbās held; others that it is Madinan and means those of the People of the Book who believed. The traditional order places the surah fifty-eighth.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ سَبَإٍ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ بِإجْماعِهِمْ وَقالَ الضَّحّاكُ، وابْنُ السّائِبِ، ومُقاتِلٌ: فِيها آيَةٌ مَدَنِيَّةٌ
سُورَةُ سَبَأٍ مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْجَمِيعِ، إِلَّا آيَةً وَاحِدَةً اخْتُلِفَ فِيهَا

setting: The men who led Makkah were rich, and they read their riches as a verdict. The surah quotes them: “We have more wealth and children, and we are not going to be punished.” It answers them directly — “It is not your wealth nor your children that bring you near to Us” — but it answers them first with two histories, set side by side.

Dāwūd and Sulaymān were given more than any man of Quraysh could imagine. For the father, the mountains and the birds were made to echo his praises, and iron was made soft so that he could fashion coats of mail. For the son, the wind ran at his command, a spring of molten copper flowed, and the jinn worked before him, building whatever he wished. The command that came with it all was: “Work, O family of Dāwūd, in gratitude. And few of My servants are grateful.” Then the surah shows how thin even that power was. Sulaymān died leaning on his staff, and the jinn went on toiling, unaware, until a creature of the earth gnawed the staff through and he fell.

Sabaʾ is the other case. Their land was a sign in itself: two gardens, to the right and to the left — “Eat of the provision of your Lord, and give thanks to Him: a good land, and a forgiving Lord.” They turned away. The flood of the dam was loosed upon them, and their gardens were exchanged for bitter fruit and tamarisk; the easy stages of their trade road were lost, and they were scattered until they became a byword. The Arabs of the Ḥijāz knew this history. Some of their own tribes traced themselves to that dispersal.

The rest of the surah presses the point home in argument. Those you call upon besides Allah do not own an atom’s weight in the heavens or the earth. On the Day, the weak and the proud will each blame the other. And the Prophet ﷺ is told to ask of his people one thing only: “that you stand up for Allah, in pairs and singly, and then reflect: there is no madness in your companion.”
aim: To show the divine power to change conditions, and the states of people under blessing — between thankfulness and ingratitude.
themes: The people of Sabaʾ and the flood
Wealth is no proof of favour
The Messenger ﷺ sent to all mankind

outline.title: Praise, and the denial of the Hour
outline.summary: Praise be to Allah, to whom belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth; His is the praise in the Hereafter. Those who disbelieve say, “The Hour will not come to us.” Say: yes, by my Lord, it will come — the Knower of the unseen, from whom not an atom’s weight escapes. They say, “Shall we show you a man who tells you that when you have been utterly torn apart, you will be in a new creation?”

outline.title: The family of Dāwūd
outline.summary: We gave Dāwūd bounty from Us: “Mountains, echo with him, and you birds.” We made iron soft for him: make full coats of mail. To Sulaymān the wind — its morning course a month, and its evening course a month — and a spring of molten copper, and jinn who worked before him. “Work, family of Dāwūd, in thanks.” When We decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death but a creature of the earth eating at his staff.

outline.title: Sabaʾ
outline.summary: For Sabaʾ there was a sign in their dwelling-place: two gardens, right and left. “A good land, and a forgiving Lord.” But they turned away, so We sent on them the flood of the dam, and gave them in place of their gardens two bearing bitter fruit. They said, “Our Lord, lengthen the distance between our journeys,” and wronged themselves; We made them tales, and scattered them utterly. Iblīs found his surmise about them true.

outline.title: Not an atom’s weight
outline.summary: Say: call on those you claim besides Allah. They do not own an atom’s weight in the heavens or the earth. Intercession avails with Him only for the one He permits — until, when terror is lifted from their hearts, they say, “What did your Lord say?” — “The truth.” Say: we or you are either upon guidance or in plain error. We have not sent you but to all mankind, as a bringer of good news and a warner.

outline.title: The followers and the leaders
outline.summary: If you could see the wrongdoers stood before their Lord, throwing the blame back and forth. The weak will say to the proud, “Had it not been for you, we would have been believers.” No warner was sent to a town but its affluent said: “We have more wealth and children, and we shall not be punished.” It is not your wealth nor your children that bring you near to Us. Whatever you spend, He will replace it.

outline.title: One thing
outline.summary: When Our clear ayat are recited to them they say, “This is only a man who wants to turn you from what your fathers worshipped.” Say: I exhort you to one thing only — that you stand for Allah, in twos and singly, and then reflect (34:46). Say: I ask of you no wage. Say: the truth has come, and falsehood neither begins anything nor brings it back. If you could see when they are terrified, with no escape, and seized from a place near at hand.

keyAyah.why: The command given to the most favoured household in history — and the observation that follows it: few of My servants are grateful.

virtues.text: “When Allah decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His word, with a sound like a chain upon smooth rock. When terror is lifted from their hearts they say: ‘What did your Lord say?’ They say: ‘The truth; and He is the Most High, the Great.’”

before: Al-Aḥzāb ended with man taking up the Trust. Sabaʾ shows two peoples entrusted with great blessings, and what each made of them.
after: Sabaʾ opens “Praise be to Allah, to whom belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth.” Fāṭir opens “Praise be to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth” — and goes on to the same theme: remember the favour of Allah upon you.
